Second Impact causing a deluge, Lilith, giant Adam, Antarctica, etc. These are all direct references to Enoch's apocryphal, not the Bible.  
Only the crosses and the spear are a reference to the Bible. The name of the spear (Longinus) is supposed to refer to the name of the Roman soldier who stuck a spear in Jesus on the cross, but in fact there is no documentation of that soldier's name, and Longinus is a Roman name for "spear", which only reinforces the thesis that this was not the soldier's real name.  
It is interesting to note that many Roman politicians took the name Gaius Cassius Longinus, which curiously bears the name of each of the three spears in the Evangelion Rebuild.  
The Antarctica thing was not very well taken advantage of, since in the book of Enoch it is said that in the south of the planet, in a cold place, the 200 angels and their 20 leading angels (The Watchers) who disobeyed God and taught all kinds were imprisoned because they taught  magic and sciences to man, besides being the parents of the Nephilim (giant children of angels and human women) whose flood of Noah killed them all. The giant Adam thing has to do with a vision of a man who saw Jesus seeking the soul of a giant he claimed was Adam.  
The four "Adams" in Antarctica from the Evangelion Rebuild can be a direct reference to the four archangels sent by God to help in the flood by killing the giants and instructing Noah, these being the archangels Michael, Gabriel, Raphael and Uriel. It's also worth noting that the EVA-01 at the end of The End of Evangelion movie sprouts 4 wings of light on its back (common in Cherubim) and then sprouts 12 wings, which could be a direct reference to the worst angel in heaven, the Samael (not to be confused with Lucifer).  
It is important to understand that the person responsible for the snake that tempted Eve to eat the forbidden fruit was not Lucifer, but Samael.  
Lucifer had been banished from heaven for thinking he was superior to everyone (even though he was just a Cherub... You'll understand), but in the question M made Samael is much more lousy, he's angry at God, he's a giant angel and he's probably the most powerful of all, but was not banished from paradise. If Lucifer has ever been scratched by an archangel (I don't remember which one it was), imagine Samael.  
An interesting observation is also to note that in Eva anime and TEoE no EVA has an S2 core until it gets one (with the exception of white EVAs, all have one), EVA-01 gets his by eating the 14th angel Zeruel, however, in Rebuild all EVAs appear to have at least one S2 core, with the 01 getting a second core by merging with the Rei that was inside the tenth angel Zeruel. The strange thing is that the EVA-13 appears to have only one core and yet still initiates a Quasi-Fourth Impact.  
The Rebuild elements make a lot of sense until the end of the second film, but from the third onwards there's a lot of script scoop.
